payload.body: Spectral-median (median frequency) is the full-spectrum energy-quantile summary that reports the frequency f_med at which half of the total spectral energy lies below and half above. Parameters: (1) the per-bin energy vector E = {E_i} over the full analyzed spectrum [f0, f_max), (2) the energy-weighted cumulative distribution C(f) = (sum of E_i for bins at frequency <= f) / (sum of all E_i), (3) the target quantile q, which the median fixes at q = 0.5; the reported value is the smallest frequency f such that C(f) >= q. It is a member of the same quantile family as spectral-rolloff, which fixes q at the 85% energy level: the median is the 50% level of that family and does not depend on a chosen high-level contour. It reads the full per-bin energy vector and carries no [f_low, f_high) band bounds, so it is a full-side summary rather than a band-local one. Persists as a standard energy-quantile summary in audio analysis, computed on the per-bin energy vector in MIR toolkits and reported in sound-description documentation. [formal: mediana spectri | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

payload.body: Cepstral-mean-variance normalization (CMVN) is a signal processing technique that normalizes cepstral coefficient vectors by computing the mean and variance across an utterance (or a sliding window) and applying z-score normalization to each frame. Parameters: (1) the mean is computed per coefficient dimension across all frames, (2) the variance is computed per coefficient dimension across all frames, (3) the normalization is applied element-wise as (c_i - μ_i) / σ_i for each coefficient c_i, where σ_i is the standard deviation. The technique removes both channel-induced mean shifts and variance mismatches between speakers. Persistence mechanism: implemented as a standard preprocessing step in speech recognition pipelines (Kaldi, HTK) and encoded in audio processing libraries (Python, MATLAB). payload.body: Jitter (period perturbation) is a voice-quality parameter quantifying the cycle-to-cycle variation of the fundamental period in a voiced speech signal. For N consecutive glottal cycles with periods P_i, the perturbation is computed as APQ1 = (1/(N-1)) * Σ_i |P_{i+1} - P_i| / ((1/N) * Σ_i P_i), or equivalently the standard deviation of the periods divided by their mean, reported in percent or in absolute units (milliseconds or seconds). Parameters: (1) the voiced speech signal segmented at pitch-synchronous cycle boundaries, (2) the per-cycle period measure, (3) the perturbation variant (APQ1 — average absolute difference, JRR — ratio, JDP — absolute difference). Small jitter indicates period stability (normal phonation); large jitter indicates period instability (dysphonia). Persistence mechanism: the standardized clinical voice-quality parameter computed by acoustic analysis software (Praat, laryngology toolkits) from pitch-synchronous period tracks; it persists as a documented measurement in voice-disorder assessment. [formal: titubatio | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.02]

payload.body: Electroglottography (EGG) is a non-invasive technique that measures glottal vocal-fold contact over time by passing a small alternating current through the vocal folds and recording the voltage across them. Because the glottal contact area modulates the electrical impedance of the vocal folds — high impedance when the glottis is open (air gap), low impedance when the folds are in contact — the peak-to-peak amplitude of the voltage is inversely related to glottal contact area, and its demodulated envelope, the electroglottogram (EGG waveform), tracks the open/close cycle of the glottis. Parameters: (1) excitation current — a small AC current kept below the safety threshold (typically ~0.5 mA peak at ~2.5 kHz); (2) electrode placement — two submental/neck electrodes completing the current path through the larynx; (3) demodulation — per-cycle peak-to-peak voltage measurement producing a continuous signal; (4) output — the electroglottogram, a time series whose amplitude is inversely proportional to glottal contact area. Persistence mechanism: standardized EGG transducers and laryngeal analysis systems (Kay PENTAGRAM, the laryngograph), documented in clinical laryngology and voice-disorder assessment; the waveform persists as a measured time series of glottal contact. Electroglottography (EGG) is a non-invasive technique that measures glottal vocal-fold contact over time by passing a small alternating current through the vocal folds and recording the voltage across them. Because the glottal contact area modulates the electrical impedance of the vocal folds — high impedance when the glottis is open (air gap), low impedance when the folds are in contact — the peak-to-peak amplitude of the voltage is inversely related to glottal contact area, and its demodulated envelope, the electroglottogram (EGG waveform), tracks the open/close cycle of the glottis. Parameters: (1) excitation current — a small AC current kept below the safety threshold (typically ~0.5 mA peak at ~2.5 kHz); (2) electrode placement — two submental/neck electrodes completing the current path through the larynx; (3) demodulation — per-cycle peak-to-peak voltage measurement producing a continuous signal; (4) output — the electroglottogram, a time series whose amplitude is inversely proportional to glottal contact area. Persistence mechanism: standardized EGG transducers and laryngeal analysis systems (Kay PENTAGRAM, the laryngograph), documented in clinical laryngology and voice-disorder assessment; the waveform persists as a measured time series of glottal contact. The cepstral-domain is constructed by: (1) computing the power spectrum of a signal, (2) taking the log of each frequency bin's magnitude, (3) applying the inverse Fourier transform. Removing the power-spectrum construct eliminates step 1 of this construction, stopping the cepstral-domain from being formed. DEPENDS_ON is distinct from the accepted DERIVED_FROM edge: the domain not only historically derives from power-spectrum analysis but structurally requires it as a necessary input.
